questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Our plane / arrived at / the Mumbai airport / at the right time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the use of the definite article 'the' is incorrect.
 
• In sentences where the name of the airport is mentioned, the **definite article 'the'** is typically not used.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be **'Mumbai airport'** instead of **'the Mumbai airport'**.

Hence, the correct sentence is: ***Our plane arrived at Mumbai airport at the right time*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When referring to a specific airport by its name, the **definite article 'the'** is usually omitted.

 
 
• **Example:** *He is flying to Los Angeles International Airport*.
 
 
 
• However, when referring to an airport in a general sense without its specific name, the **definite article 'the'** can be used.
 
 
• **Example:** *He is waiting at the airport*.

questions.question:
Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options.

This is the story of eight round planets, the few rocks in between, and some comets.

options.text: This is the story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, and some comets.
This is the story of eight round planets, a few rocks in between, and some comets
This is a story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, and some comets.
This is story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, and some comets.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word 'few' is used to denote an indefinite, small number of rocks, but it should be 'a few' to indicate a small number of rocks specifically.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence should be: *This is the story of eight round planets, a few rocks in between, and some comets.*

Hence, the correct statement is: ***This is the story of eight round planets, a few rocks in between, and some comets.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **'a few'** is used to indicate a small number of something, which is not zero, but not many.
 
• The term **'few'** generally implies almost none, which is not the intended meaning in the given sentence.

questions.question:

Everyone have/ to join health orientation/ classes before/ going for trekking.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the plural form of the verb 'have' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject **'Everyone'** is **singular**.
 
• The verb should agree with the singular subject, thus the **singular form of the verb** should be used.
 
 
• **Example:** ***Everyone has** the right to speak*.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'has' should be used in place of the plural form 'have'.

 

Hence, the correct statement is: ***Everyone has__ to join health orientation classes before going for trekking*.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It was noticed / that he truthful / answered the questions / raised by the Headmistress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the fourth part of the given sentence, the adjective form 'truthful' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be the adverb form 'truthfully', as it describes the verb 'answered'.
 
• **Example:** *He truthfully answered the questions.*

Hence, the correct statement is: ***It was noticed that he truthfully __answered the questions raised by the Headmistress*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Adjectives describe nouns, while adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
 
• Using the correct form ensures that the sentence is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** *She is a **quick** runner.* (adjective describing the noun 'runner')
 
• **Example:** *She runs **quickly**.* (adverb describing the verb 'runs')

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She __finished her quickly breakfast__ and rushed to school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Finished her breakfast quickly"** accurately and grammatically places the adverb **"quickly"** to describe the manner in which she finished her breakfast.
 
• This option ensures that the subject** "She" **and the verb **"finished"** are correctly aligned, maintaining clear** subject-verb agreement.**
 
• It logically orders the sentence, making it easy to understand that she finished eating her breakfast in a quick manner.
 
• The structure adheres to standard English.
 
 
• **syntax: subject + verb + object + adverb.**
 
 
 
• Placing** "quickly"** after **"breakfast"** avoids **misplaced modifiers and ensures that "quickly" modifies how she finished her breakfast.**
 
• This construction provides a** natural, fluent reading experience, enhancing readability.**

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Her breakfast finished quickly" **incorrectly suggests that the breakfast itself is performing the action of finishing.
 
• **"Quickly her breakfast finished" **is awkward and does not follow standard English syntax; it also implies the breakfast is finishing itself.
 
• **"Finished breakfast hers quickly"** is ungrammatical and incorrectly orders the possessive pronoun and breakfast.
